author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Playstation 2 Dev - Faster 2D Graphics in C and Benchmarking
summary: Tom Marks benchmarks a PS2 homebrew 2D renderer while moving its performance-critical implementation from Lua into C, preserving the higher-level Lua API and testing whether the language boundary changes real example workloads.

blocks.text: This development stream exposes an optimization decision in progress rather than showing only a finished engine. The stated plan keeps the existing Lua-facing API but ports important drawing logic to C, then compares the example programs for improvement. That separation is instructive: an accessible scripting layer can remain part of the tool design while inner loops, command construction or data handling move closer to the native PS2SDK environment. The linked repository lets viewers inspect the code instead of inferring everything from the final screen.

A livestream benchmark can contain changing builds, debugging pauses and measurement noise; its notes offer no compact table of scenes, compiler flags or repeated run statistics. A speedup also cannot be assigned to “C versus Lua” in the abstract without identifying which work crossed the boundary and which allocations or calls disappeared. Treat the session as a transparent optimization case study. Reproduce the same examples from the linked revision before carrying its result into a different renderer or game architecture.
